run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:32:23Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate alert is explained by a failure on the frontend→ad call path, and the fault-applying object the evidence shows is a chaos-mesh Schedule that repeatedly injected JVM chaos into the ad pod. Frontend-proxy's own error spans (operations ingress and router frontend egress) were at a background level of ~0.004–0.03 per second until the 01:33:23 sample, then climbed to 0.52/s at 01:34:23, 1.537/s at 01:37:23 and 1.958/s at 01:40:23; the alert's stated value 1.5333 matches the level observed around 01:37:23 rather than the 01:32:23 anchor, when the measured rate was ~0.0037/s. The error spans are confined to the ad path: frontend's own error spans are on GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data and the grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client span, whose errors rise from 0 to ~0.99/s while its non-error spans fall to 0; failed GetAds spans are fast (78% ≤2 ms, 88% ≤100 ms), and the ad service's own server spans (oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, getAdsByCategory, getRandomAds) fall to 0 from the 01:37:23 sample. On the ad pod, the ad container was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 01:31:52 with a 450Mi memory limit after its working set jumped from ~309 MB to ~420 MB, restarted once, and has produced no log lines after 01:31:49; the pod reports Ready only because it defines no liveness/readiness/startup probe. In the chaos-mesh namespace, a Schedule named otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos began spawning JVMChaos experiments against otel-demo/ad-554b849958-fcl25/ad at 01:31:17, with 'Successfully apply chaos' events about 10 s after each start and Recovered/TimeUp about 55 s later, through at least 01:40:24; the frontend GetAds error rise begins inside the second such experiment. The exact JVMChaos action cannot be read because chaos-mesh custom resources are not an allowed kind, so the causal link between the injected JVM fault and ad's failure to serve is a hypothesis, not an observed fact; flagd's adFailure/adHighCpu/adManualGc flags are all 'off' as configured, which argues against a flagd-driven fault, and Jaeger holds no traces for the incident window, so the gRPC status code and error text of the failing GetAds calls remain unknown.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error spans rose from a background level to a sustained failure: summed 5-minute error rate was ~0.0037–0.03/s through the 01:33:23 sample, 0.52/s at 01:34:23, 1.537/s at 01:37:23, 1.958/s at 01:40:23 and 1.4198/s at 01:43:00; at the 01:32:23 alert anchor the frontend-proxy ingress error rate was 0.0037/s and the router frontend egress error rate 0.

The frontend service's own error rate rose in the same window: frontend summed error-span rate went from 0 at the 01:35:23 sample to 1.685/s at 01:34:23-range samples, 3.070/s and 3.274/s, peaking 3.983/s at 01:40:23 and 2.468/s at 01:43:23, while accounting, checkout, payment and recommendation stayed at 0 and ad stayed at ~0.0037/s.

Frontend error spans are concentrated on the ad path: the error rate of span_name 'GET /api/data', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' all rise to ~0.99/s, 'GET' rises similarly, and 'tcp.connect' rises to ~0.017–0.048/s, while 'GET /api/cart', 'POST /api/cart', 'POST /api/checkout', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem', 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and the product-catalog calls stay at 0.

Frontend's client spans for grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds flipped from non-error to error: STATUS_CODE_UNSET was 0.73–0.94/s through the 01:35:23 sample, fell to 0.0148/s at 01:37:23 and 0 from 01:39:23, while STATUS_CODE_ERROR rose from 0 to 0.411/s at 01:35:23, 0.756/s at 01:37:23 and 0.99/s at 01:41:23.

The failing GetAds spans are short: of a total error rate of 0.886/s at 01:42:00, 0.781/s is at or below 2 ms, 0.816/s at or below 6 ms and 0.858/s at or below 100 ms, i.e. the calls fail quickly rather than by long timeout.

The ad service's own spans stopped: oteldemo.AdService/GetAds fell from 0.837/s at the 01:34:23 sample to 0.337/s at 01:35:23 and 0 from 01:37:23 onward, and getAdsByCategory and getRandomAds fell to 0 in the same samples; the ad service's flagd.* spans also fell to 0.

Pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 (namespace otel-demo, owner ReplicaSet ad-554b849958) is Running and Ready with restartCount 1, and its container 'ad' previous instance terminated with reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, startedAt 2026-11-18T00:54:51Z and finishedAt 2026-11-18T01:31:52Z; the pod's Ready condition lastTransitionTime is 2026-11-18T01:31:53Z.

Kubelet events for ad-554b849958-fcl25 are only Normal and record the restart: images already present (Pulled, count 2, last 01:31:52), 'Created container: ad' (count 2, last 01:31:52) and 'Started container ad' (count 2, last 01:31:53); no Unhealthy, Evicted or FailedScheduling event for this pod was returned.

The ad container was near its memory ceiling before the OOM: container_memory_working_set_bytes for the pre-restart container (id a9304b54…) was ~304–312 MB from 01:10 to 01:31, then 420 MB at 01:32:00; the current container (id ed742b64…) starts at 2.6 MB at 01:32:00 and grows to 165 MB at 01:34, 214 MB at 01:36, 245 MB at 01:38 and 282 MB at 01:42. The deployment sets limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi and requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi.

The ad pod defines no livenessProbe, readinessProbe or startupProbe on its single container 'ad' (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad), so its Ready=True condition does not demonstrate that the application is serving.

The ad Service's endpoints still contain the pod: Endpoints 'ad' has address 100.96.4.112:8080 with targetRef Pod ad-554b849958-fcl25, matching the ClusterIP Service 'ad' selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad on port 8080.

In namespace chaos-mesh, Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos spawned JVMChaos experiments against otel-demo/ad-554b849958-fcl25/ad repeatedly: Spawned at 01:31:17, 01:32:17, 01:33:28, 01:34:24, 01:35:20, 01:36:17, 01:37:30, 01:38:27, 01:39:25 and 01:40:24, each with 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-fcl25/ad' about 4–10 s later (first at 01:31:27) and 'Successfully recover chaos' roughly 45–60 s after that (first at 01:32:12), plus Warning 'Forbid spawning new job' events.

The ad container's logs stop at the restart: 1274 lines were read for the requested 01:20:00–01:43:37 range but they span only 01:30:40.941 to 01:31:49.817 ('Targeted ad request received for […]' / 'no baggage found in context'), with no lines after that; the previous container's log stream is unavailable (HTTP 400, previous terminated container not found).

In the flagd-config ConfigMap (otel-demo), the ad-related fault flags exist but are off as configured: adFailure defaultVariant 'off', adHighCpu defaultVariant 'off', adManualGc defaultVariant 'off', and every other listed flag (cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage) also defaults to 'off'.

Before the incident the same call path was healthy: traces retrieved for 00:32:23–01:25:00 (span data timestamped up to about 01:07:31) show frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 and frontend-proxy ingress/router frontend egress spans with http.status_code 200/308, and no error rows in any of the 110 spans shown.

The most consistent explanation is that the JVM chaos injected by Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos into the ad pod's JVM made the ad gRPC server stop serving, so frontend's GetAds calls fail immediately (sub-100 ms, no ad-side span or request log), frontend returns errors for /api/data, and frontend-proxy records ingress/router-egress error spans, producing the alert. The first frontend-proxy deviation appears in the 01:33:23 sample, inside the second spawned experiment (01:32:17 start, 01:32:27 applied, 01:33:28 recovered).

The ad container OOMKill at 01:31:52 may be a consequence of the same injected JVM fault (the first experiment was applied at 01:31:27, 25 s earlier, and the container's working set had just jumped from ~309 MB to ~420 MB against a 450Mi limit), and the restarted JVM may never have begun serving; this cannot be separated from the direct effect of later injections with the available evidence.

The restarted ad container's memory is climbing again (165 MB at 01:34 to 282 MB at 01:42 against a 450Mi limit), so a further OOMKill and restart of the ad pod is plausible while the pod keeps no probe that would expose an unserving JVM.

The ad service itself did not record errors: its own error-span rate stayed at ~0.0037/s (flagd EventStream/ResolveBoolean only) while frontend's GetAds client errors climbed to ~0.99/s, so the failure appears as unreachability/non-serving of ad rather than ad returning error responses on its own server spans.

Other services showed no error rise over the same range: accounting, checkout and payment stayed at 0, recommendation and fraud-detection stayed at ~0.0037–0.0046/s, and ad at ~0.0037/s, so the error burst is confined to frontend and frontend-proxy on the ad path rather than being cluster-wide.

A flagd-driven ad fault was considered and rejected as the configured cause: adFailure, adHighCpu and adManualGc (and all other demo flags) have defaultVariant 'off' in the flagd-config ConfigMap. Runtime flag overrides cannot be observed with the available sources, so this rejection applies to the configuration state that was read.

A Service/Endpoints selector mismatch was considered and rejected: Endpoints 'ad' contains the running ad pod's address 100.96.4.112:8080 and the Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad matches the pod's labels, so traffic is not being sent to a wrong or empty endpoint set.

Ask the owner of the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos (namespace chaos-mesh) to pause or delete it and to read the spawned JVMChaos resources for the injected action and target method, since that metadata was not readable here.

Check the ad container's gRPC listener on port 8080 directly, add liveness/readiness probes to the ad Deployment, and review the 450Mi memory limit together with the ad JVM heap settings, because the container OOMKilled once and its new instance is again growing toward the limit.

Validate recovery with the signals used here: frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error rate returning to 0, ad's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span rate resuming, and frontend-proxy ingress/router frontend egress error spans returning to the pre-incident background level.

gaps: The chaos-mesh custom resources are not an allowed kind, so the Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos spec and each spawned JVMChaos spec (action such as exception/latency/stress/gc, target class and method, duration, whether the schedule continued past the 01:40:24 event) could not be read; the injected fault itself was therefore not observed, only its application and recovery events.

Jaeger returned no traces for the incident window (frontend-proxy, frontend and ad searches over 01:25:00–01:43:37 and 01:30:00–01:43:37 returned no spans; the latest span data seen was about 01:07:31), so the rpc.grpc.status_code and error text of the failing GetAds calls (for example UNAVAILABLE vs another code) are unknown.

The ad container's previous (OOMKilled) log stream was unavailable (HTTP 400 previous terminated container not found) and the current instance wrote no lines after 01:31:49, so the JVM crash/startup error text and why the new instance does not serve are unknown.
The frontend pod's log query for 01:30:00–01:43:37 returned zero lines (bytes_read 0), so frontend application-level error messages for the /api/data failures could not be confirmed.
The query for NetworkPolicy objects in otel-demo returned no objects (no_data), so a network-level block of the frontend→ad path cannot be excluded from this evidence.
The ResourceQuota query returned no objects (no_data); namespace quota pressure was therefore not verified or excluded.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so who or what created or modified Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos and when is unknown.

The grouped per-service error query returned series for only accounting, ad, checkout, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, payment and recommendation; cart, currency, email, shipping, product-catalog and quote returned no series there, so their error state in this window is unknown rather than zero.
Whether flagd served runtime flag overrides differing from the ConfigMap defaults cannot be observed with the available sources; only the ConfigMap's defaultVariant values were verified.
